identity.question: Will Ukraine recapture Crimean territory by December 31, 2026?
identity.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Ukraine captures any territory in Crimea between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of Crimea is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

The border around Crimea shaded in black on the ISW map will not qualify.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date.

Any continuous shading under the following layers will qualify:
- Claimed Ukrainian Counteroffensives

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Ukraine comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded under a qualifying layer on the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Ukraine de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

current_isw_map.source: ISW Ukraine map / ArcGIS WebMap item

crimea_geometry_check.method_limit: five selected point checks only; no whole-peninsula or historical change analysis

current_isw_map.crs: top-level map WKID 102100/latestWKID3857; polygon geometries carry WKID4326 (longitude,latitude). No distance/metre calculation performed.
current_isw_map.interpretation_limit: single current map snapshot plus published feature dates; does not document changes between daily updates or criterion persistence through next update.

isw_narrative_search_result.source_title: Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 25, 2026 | ISW
isw_narrative_search_result.search_result_claims: ISW search result says geolocated footage published Sep 25 showed damage to bridge connecting occupied Crimea and Kherson Oblast after strikes in June 2026; notes reported Russian measures for Kerch Strait Bridge and routing non-essential goods via occupied southern Ukraine.
isw_narrative_search_result.source_read_status: 403 Forbidden on ordinary open; no retry/bypass

limitations: ISW map is the primary market source; map snapshot confirms currently shaded Russian-controlled terrain at selected Crimean land locations, while qualifying Ukrainian-counteroffensive persistence since market creation requires historical daily snapshots.
The search-result narrative is dated Sep 25 and reports infrastructure strikes/damage, not land recapture; its source page could not be opened (403), so only returned provider text is preserved.
No inference from absent reporting; this collection does not establish whether any qualifying event occurred at an earlier time or whether any current shading meets the market persistence rule.
No direct Crimea landing/control source beyond the ISW map was successfully captured.
